rule_text: When building or validating anything -- code, config, or process -- a point that requires a NEW decision (a judgement call, an ambiguity, something not already specified) is TERMINAL: it must not be answered inline and resumed. It is recorded as an open item and routed back into design/specification; work resumes only after the design is settled and approved. A point that instead reveals Claude's own execution error against an ALREADY-settled, already-approved design (a typo, a wrong parameter, a slip) is SELF-CORRECTABLE: Claude fixes it directly, records what was wrong and what changed, and continues -- no new approval is required, because no new decision was made. The distinguishing question is always: does resolving this require deciding something new, or only correcting execution against something already decided? A recurring decision_required outcome on the same routine, run after run, is itself a defect -- it means a threshold or parameter that should have been specified once, in config, during design, was left to be re-asked every time instead. That is a design gap to close (add the missing config), not a pattern to formalise.
enforced_by: escalation.resolution_kind (decision_required | self_correctable) for escalation-raised items -- see cfg_enum 'resolution_kind' and cfg_escalation_requirement.

rule_text: AnswerRun's flat approve/reject/revise/hold/noted vocabulary is refused for BOTH resolution_kind values -- unreachable for any dispatcher-tied escalation raised under the resolution_kind regime. decision_required must be answered through Update's richer vocabulary (ready_for_approval -> approved; -State on-hold; next_action=reject/revise/noted) -- checked and confirmed live before this half existed (escalation #820): AnswerRun silently accepted a flat 'approve' on a decision_required item, collapsing the record of a genuine judgement call into the same one-line outcome a self_correctable item gets. self_correctable must be closed via resolve-self-correctable, or converted via escalate-to-decision -- this was always the APPROVED spec (escalation-decision-vs-defect-axis-proposal-v4-20260822.md §6: 'No approve/reject/revise/hold/noted vocabulary. AnswerRun is never invoked' -- and its own §11 Stage 2 test named this exact check), never actually built or tested during #799's Stage 2 -- confirmed live the same way (escalation #822): a flat 'approve' succeeded with no refusal at all. Net effect: neither kind ever had a genuine use for AnswerRun's original 'answer and resume the same run' semantics -- decision_required runs terminate and never resume (a fresh run is the test, §5); self_correctable never carried decision vocabulary to begin with (§6).
source: researcher, 2026-08-22, escalation #795, on decision_required: "I suggest to check and test the answer to the question in the configs, my expectation is that it should not be possible and that the configs should now state that." The self_correctable half was already in the approved proposal (v4 §6/§11 Stage 2) but never built or tested in #799 -- found checking the first half, not separately instructed.

The mirror-image guard, update()'s own dispatcher carve-out (refuses UNLESS resolution_kind='decision_required'), already existed from #798/#799 and is unchanged.

rule_text: Each module or utility, from now on (case-by-case as it comes up in development, NOT retrofitted to existing modules), must have a test plan. The test plan covers every meaningfully different interaction, parameter, and option combination of that module/utility's intended functionality -- not a single happy-path example. The test plan is a living artifact: when a functional component changes, the test plan for that component is updated in the same unit of work, before the change is considered complete -- the same 'same unit of work' discipline governance.build_md_on_code_change already applies to BUILD.md. The test plan is RUN after the design is approved and the build (per the approved plan) is complete -- a required stage inside the existing plan/propose/design (in detail) -> approve -> build per the plan -> approve cycle, not a separate optional step. The test results are included IN the build's escalation resolution when requesting final approval -- not just claimed as 'tested live' in prose without the actual per-case results shown, and not omitted. Origin: escalation #795, where the approved proposal's own named Stage 2 test ('self_correctable has no reachable AnswerRun path') was written into the design document but never actually run before the build was reported complete -- twice, once for each half of the same function. A written-but-unexecuted test is indistinguishable from no test at all.

enforced_by: No automated check yet -- deliberately, per the researcher's case-by-case rollout instruction (building a configmaint.validate check now, before any real test plan exists to check against, would be exactly the 'machinery-heavy design' simple-steps-not-engineered-designs warns against). Practical enforcement today is manual: the next module/utility design proposal should name its test plan as part of the design, and the build's resolution should carry the test plan's actual results. A configmaint.validate check (e.g. 'every active cfg_utility/cfg_work_package has an associated test plan reference') is a natural candidate to add once the first real test plan exists and its storage convention (table vs doc) is chosen against that real case -- not designed speculatively here.

rule_text: An escalation item sitting at next_action_assigned_to=Claude in an open working state (review/in-progress) has exactly ONE legitimate way to hand it to the Researcher: set next_action=ready_for_approval together with next_action_assigned_to=Researcher and a resolution, all in the SAME call -- whether the resolution states a completed fix awaiting approval, or an open question needing the researcher's decision on how to proceed. There is no separate bare-reassignment/bounce-back-via-review path any more (researcher, 2026-09-03: caught this exact bare-reassign loop recurring on #1373/#1316/#1366/#1375 -- their prior existence as a documented but unenforced two-branch rule left room for the wrong branch to keep getting chosen). The same applies to an item Claude finds itself unsure whether to apply even after approval (state=approved): reset it via Correction to next_action=ready_for_approval, next_action_assigned_to=Researcher, with the conflict stated plainly in the resolution. Before any hand-over for approval (escalation #2178, 2026-10-21), Claude checks three things and the hand-over states them: (1) what exactly the researcher is asked to approve; (2) that it is ready for approval, i.e. a finished piece of work or a decision with its options, not something Claude still has to do or work the researcher has told Claude to carry; (3) the resolution states plainly what approval is sought. If none of the three holds, the item is not handed over: work already under way stays with Claude with a one-line acknowledgement, and clearing the Stop-hook backlog check is never a reason to hand over. An interim approval (approval of one step whose result needs a further action by Claude) is handed over with -NeedsFollowup 1 in the same call, so the researcher's `approved` routes the item back to Claude (re-assigned) and does not close a step still in progress (escalation #1075 mechanism).

rule_text: Cluster allocation (cluster_strong) is a loose association for the purposes of analysis. A strand or unit that finds a word associated with another cluster records that association in its ledger, for cross-cluster analysis. It never proposes, raises or applies a re-tag or re-allocation of a single word, and never builds option tables for one. Exception: re-tagging takes place only in exceptional circumstances, where a group of words turns out to be wrongly clustered (example: #2163, the body words and the flesh word's own T-codes moved to M47 on the researcher's instruction).

rule_text: Before any query in a strand or unit, use what is already extracted. (1) The strand folder's existing pulls come first: their columns (other_m_words, narrative_refs, hit_words, group) are aggregated from the file, not re-queried. (2) The verse to M-code link is verse_lexical.strong joined to cluster_strong (cluster_code LIKE 'M%', deleted=0). For any verse set it is read with ONE set-based query over that set. Never a per-verse query loop, and never a pass over every cluster to find which apply. (3) Results already produced in this or another strand (ledgers, face-combination CSVs, crossrefs, reading placements) are reused, not re-derived. (4) A query that does not return within seconds is a signal the approach is wrong: stop and re-plan, do not wait it out.

rule_text: The study's primary focus is the human inner being (HIB). Each verse in a strand is routed by what it shows, and the route is recorded in the ledger. (A) Other beings in their own right: a word used of God, angels, other spirits or nature (non-HIB) is routed to Ch 13 "Other beings" (13.1 Divine, 13.2 Angels, 13.3 Other spirits, 13.4 Nature), analysed for what the verses say that being is and does; for God, also how his character passed to the HIB through creation in his image, held open (not deep-dived now, #1984). (B) Another being interacting with the HIB is fully in HIB scope and follows the HIB analytic pattern. A verse may take A and B, described from different angles. (C) A verse with no inner-being and no other-being bearing is still properly assessed in the analysis and recorded in the ledger, but does not enter the narrative. Existing analysis and narrative sections are NOT corrected in a dedicated pass: each is reset only on the researcher's individual instruction. Routing a strand's verses into the narrative waits for the researcher's direction.

rule_text: A strand pulls verses by its M-code, but an M-code tag does not make a word the verse's characteristic: cluster allocation is a loose association (rule 70) and a word's role -- characteristic, qualifier / process-element, or standalone -- is decided per occurrence (verse-analysis method s13-14; glossary 'role'). Each verse is read in its passage and genre; every M-coded word (rule 71, set-based) is given its role against the verse's main IB operation; only then is the strand's own word read, in the role it has there. A strand word in the qualifier role is carried as a qualifier of that characteristic (no own account from that verse, method s13b), recorded as an interrelationship and a face (#1919), and the verse's home follows the characteristic. The M-code words are read in relation to each other (relational observation), pointers outside the verse kept separate, parties and route recorded (rule 72), following the confirmed role-driven sequence (#1704) and progressive reading across strands (#1706). Collections are grouped by main operation, not entry word. Existing narrative is not audited in a dedicated pass; placements are corrected in each strand's read-back as the verse's characteristic M-code comes into focus. Full guide: Workflow/Instructions/wa-verse-reading-by-role-guide-v2-20261019.md. Amended 2026-10-19 (#2168): (1) read outward from the verse, not inward from the item's question -- first write down everything the verse carries, each with where it bears (chapter, thread, signpost), and answer the item's question last; (2) for every word that names an inner or bodily act, look at the original -- the root's range (strong_meaning_tree and the ESV renderings across its verses) and whether the English adds or hides something; (3) an item or verse is never closed on 'not X' -- the close records what the verse is instead. A role label is never a verdict.

rule_text: The open threads register is carried in the escalation table as type='thread' (alias OT-nn), not edited as a markdown file. A thread is not worked as a task: it moves only when a strand reaches it (focused capture, #1900). Its items (escalation_thread_item; cluster, Strong's, verse, strand, chapter, event, researcher, escalation) are what a strand or task is matched against (Escalation.ps1 -Action Match). Claude manages each thread's lifecycle; the researcher gives feedback in chat, which Claude records verbatim the same turn, and there is no approval step (researcher 2026-10-12: 'the rest you need to control'). Every response to an item -- touched, narrowed, forward, ruling, note, closed, reopened, withdrawn, superseded -- is an escalation_thread_item_response row, recorded through Escalation.ps1 -Action Update -Id OT-nn -Item ... -ResponseKind ... -Respond ..., and written in full to the thread's history ('all interaction must go to history'). A thread completes when its last open item is settled; a thread is withdrawn or superseded (-SupersededBy OT-nn) with its open items settled in the same call. Notes and comments on a thread are Updates, never edits to the register file (rule T8). New held items and researcher questions are raised as threads at ledger approval. The file _analytics/cross-cluster-web/open-threads-register.md is generated (Escalation.ps1 -Action Export -Type thread) and regenerated at session-close when a thread row changed in the session (SC12, #2173). Its quality, validity and integrity are audited at every start (Escalation.ps1 -Action ThreadAudit, #2173 P5).

rule_text: Every narrative statement that goes beyond its verses has a narrative claim register entry with verse sources, or it is removed from the narrative (it may return later in another form). The interpretation of verses in context sets the narrative; verses that sit against a narrative line change the narrative and get their own claim, never trimmed, set aside or left out. Readings of the words in focus check the full verse set: a verse in neither the narrative nor the register is a missing reading area. The register anchors what verses say from different readings and focal points; the narrative tells the story from the claims; the register keeps the narrative honest. When an update touches a chapter, the existing passages on the concept being updated and its related concepts (not the whole chapter) are read against the register under this rule in the same pass, and that concept's current claims that no passage tells are linked, restated or withdrawn (researcher 2026-10-15, #2148/#2152).
